test_title: PYST 23: SSC CGL 2024 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On: 19 Sept, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: maths
question: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 200 metres. When the policeman starts the chase, the thief also starts running. If the speed of the thief is 9 km/h and that of the policeman 10 km/h, how far will the thief have to run before he is overtaken?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of speeds of Policeman to Thief = 10 : 9

Since the time taken is constant, ratio of distances covered = 10 : 9

Difference in distance ratio = 1 unit = 200 m = 0.2 km

Distance covered by thief = 9 units = 9 × 0.2 = 1.8 km

**∴ The correct answer is 1.8 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of Policeman = 10 km/h

Speed of Thief = 9 km/h

Initial distance between them = 200 m = 0.2 km

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d9130cb192aad85372295fb97f65dbd03cc5122348146ef8fe519eb387a7a245.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed = Speed of A − Speed of B (in same direction)

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative speed = 10 − 9 = 1 km/h

⇒ Time taken to catch the thief = 0.2 km ÷ 1 km/h = 0.2 h

⇒ Distance covered by thief before being caught = Speed of Thief × Time

⇒ Distance = 9 km/h × 0.2 h = 1.8 km

**∴ The correct answer is 1.8 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their speeds (V₁ − V₂). When moving in opposite directions, it is the sum of their speeds (V₁ + V₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert a speed from km/h to m/s, multiply the value by 5 ÷ 18. Conversely, to convert from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18 ÷ 5.

Average Speed

When equal distances are covered at different speeds x and y, the average speed for the entire journey is given by (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).
